newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BOON HAMMERS FIRST HUNDRED FOR DURHAM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BOON HAMMERS FIRST HUNDRED FOR DURHAM.

text.p: Former Australian test batsman David Boon hammered his first century for Durham on Wednesday as the struggling English county pulled off a rare victory.
Boon, captaining Durham in his debut season on the county circuit, struck 103 off 133 deliveries to set up a 64-run win over Northamptonshire in the Benson and Hedges Cup.
Durham's success at Chester-le-Street in the group stage of the 50 overs Cup was only their second victory in their last 43 games in all competitions.
Boon, who hit eight fours and shared a third wicket stand of 103 in 27 overs with opener Jon Lewis (47), was out in the last over of the innings, which ended with Durham on 225 for six.

They defended the modest total effectively thanks to some incisive swing and seam bowling by left-armer Simon Brown, who had a burst of three wickets in four balls in his six for 30 as Northants were 161 all out.
Boon hailed Durham's victory as a "great team effort".
The Tasmanian said: "We have talked about how we can press (the advantage) home when we get into winning positions and today we put it into practice. The beauty of it was that we made things happen."
One day after Ireland pulled off their first Cup win over an English county by beating Middlesex, the British Universities sprung another surprise.
They beat Sussex by 19 runs at Cambridge, only the students fourth win since all universities were included in the competition in 1987 instead of just Oxford and Cambridge.
Defending a moderate 217 for six on a good batting pitch, the Universities seemed to be heading for defeat as Sussex reached 110 for one in 27 overs.

But doubts began to creep in as Steffan Jones bowled his 10 overs and took one for 22 and then when Sussex tried to accelerate, occasional bowler Mark Chilton snapped up a decisive five for 26 as the county slumped to 198 all out.
A match-winning 112 not out by Kim Barnett spurred Derbyshire to a six-wicket win at Old Trafford over holders Lancashire, whose defeat left them struggling to qualify for the quarter-finals.
Needing 224 to win, Derbyshire were guided home with nine balls to spare under the influence of Barnett's cool resolve in an innings containing 10 fours.
It was the first time Lancashire - beaten by Yorkshire on Tuesday - had suffered successive defeats in the competition since 1981.
All-rounder Matthew Fleming captured his second five-wicket haul with his medium pacers in consecutive Cup games to help Kent beat Hampshire by two wickets at Canterbury.
Fleming followed his five wickets against Surrey on Monday with five for 27 as Hampshire were restricted to 207 all out.
Opener Matthew Walker (83) and Nigel Llong (55) hit their best scores in the competition, sharing a stand of 72 in 12 overs to ensure Kent got home at 211 for eight with 4.2 overs left.
Surrey, powered by 66 in 49 balls from opener Alistair Brown and a run-a-ball 69 from all-rounder Ben Hollioake, overcame Gloucestershire's formidable 280 for seven at Bristol.
With all-rounder Chris Lewis hitting an unbeaten 35, and adding 37 in five overs with the injured Mark Butcher, Surrey secured victory at 282 for seven with four balls remaining.
